newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU asks experts to break European company deadlock.
newsitem.headline: EU asks experts to break European company deadlock.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it had appointed a group of labour experts to try to break a long deadlock over legislation that would allow firms to set up as "European" companies rather than national ones.

The European Company Statute, first proposed by the Commission more than 20 years ago, has been blocked by a conflict between European Union governments over provisions on worker involvement in company decisions.

The Commission said it had appointed Etienne Davignon, president of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique and a former European Commissioner, to head a six-member group that would propose a solution.
The conflict has pitted Germany, which wants to impose its own system of worker participation on company boards, against Britain, which opposes any mandatory rules.

The EU has come under increasing pressure from industry to close what is seen as a big gap in its effort to create a single market -- the inability of companies with operations in different member states to form a single legal entity under EU law.

The experts have been asked to devise a solution that would also apply to proposals to create a European association, European cooperative society and European mutual society, also blocked by the worker-participation dispute.
They have been asked to produce a report by early 1997.

The other group members are Rolf Thuesing, a member of the executive committee of the German employers' confederation BDA; Silvana Sciarra, labour law professor at the University of Florence; Alain Viandier, law professor at the University of Paris V; Hans Berger, president of the Federation of Mining and Energy Institute of the German trade unions federation DGB; and Evelyne Pichot, a French consultant.
